Coaches like Dan Quinn and voices including Robert Griffin III and Pat McAfee praised the raw effort, calling it a career-defining splash play that highlights Owens' value on special teams, where he logged 84 percent of snaps last season.

news.hook: Tyler Owens bulled through two blockers and slammed Britain Covey to the turf on a punt coverage—a raw, explosive hit that had coaches raving and fans editing him as the Hulk.
news.name: Commanders' Tyler Owens Hulk-Smashes Eagles Punt Returner in Week 1 Thriller
news.summary: In the Washington Commanders' tight 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, special teams standout Tyler Owens powered past a double team for a highlight hit that coach Dan Quinn called one of his favorite special teams plays in years. Owens shrugged off the buzz, saying it was just what he does, while Robert Griffin III praised it as the kind of splash play that builds NFL careers. Rookie linebacker Sonny Styles shone too, notching 4 tackles, 2 for loss, a sack, and a QB hit in his debut, giving fans bright spots despite the defeat.

news.hook: J.J. Watt settles into the top analyst spot next to Jim Nantz, calling key early games while Tony Romo stays off the schedule amid his leave.
news.name: CBS Keeps J.J. Watt in Top NFL Booth for Weeks 2 and 3, No Romo Return
news.summary: CBS Sports announced its NFL broadcast teams for Weeks 2 and 3, with Watt, Nantz, and Tracy Wolfson handling the Patriots-Steelers game on Sept. 20 and Ravens-Cowboys from Rio on Sept. 27. Romo remains absent following his July arrest on an operating while intoxicated charge, to which he pleaded no contest earlier this month, and CBS has shared no return timeline. Other crews feature voices like Kevin Harlan on Chiefs-Dolphins and Ian Eagle on Bengals-Steelers, as the network relies on Watt's solid early performances. Fans showed excitement for matchups like the top team in Pittsburgh, blending anticipation with speculation on Romo's future.

news.hook: Jalen Hurts led the Eagles to a win with three touchdowns and key scrambles, yet faced sharp criticism. Meanwhile, Justin Herbert got more leniency after the Chargers' loss.
news.name: Fans Call Out Double Standards in Jalen Hurts and Justin Herbert Criticism
news.summary: In Week 1, Hurts completed 14 of 25 passes for 203 yards and three touchdowns, plus 46 rushing yards, securing Philadelphia's 24-22 victory over Washington despite some offensive struggles. Herbert finished 17 of 27 for 209 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Los Angeles' 26-14 upset loss to Arizona amid penalties and miscues. Social media highlighted contrasting takes, with Hurts called out harshly while blame shifted from Herbert, prompting accusations of inconsistent standards and some claims of racial bias.

news.hook: Jalen Hurts threw three touchdown passes in the Eagles' new offense, but ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky's 'fine' label had fans firing back right away.
news.name: Eagles Edge Commanders 24-22, Orlovsky Calls Offense 'Fine'
news.summary: Philadelphia kicked off the 2026 NFL season with a 24-22 win over Washington, thanks to Hurts completing 14 of 25 passes for 203 yards and three scores, plus 48 rushing yards including a crucial 22-yard scramble. Tight end Dallas Goedert grabbed two touchdowns, rookie Dontayvion Wicks scored in his debut, and the defense stopped a late two-point try. Orlovsky described the effort as 'solid' with room to grow in coordinator Sean Mannion's Shanahan-inspired scheme, drawing pushback from fans who see higher potential after last year's Super Bowl run and insist the team will rack up wins.

news.hook: With the clock ticking down, Darnell Washington caught the ball and planted Falcons safety Xavier Watts into the turf with a stiff arm that looked straight out of basketball.
news.name: Darnell Washington's Vicious Stiff Arm Steals Steelers' Win Over Falcons
news.summary: In the Steelers' 20-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, tight end Darnell Washington sealed the win late in the fourth quarter with a 15-yard catch and a brutal stiff arm on third-and-three. The 6-foot-7 powerhouse, often called 'Mount Washington,' sent Watts flying, prompting teammate Pat Freiermuth to say from across the field, 'This is not gonna be good for that kid. He dirted him into the ground.' Fans lit up timelines calling it the stiff arm of the week, with jokes about dribbling a defender like a basketball, turning the play into the game's defining highlight despite Washington's modest two catches for 18 yards.

news.hook: Zay Flowers dazzled with 150 yards and a touchdown before a hamstring tweak sent him to the sideline early. The Ravens still cruised to victory, showcasing their new defensive edge.
news.name: Ravens Dominate Colts 41-23 in Minter's Debut Behind Pass Rush and Flowers' Big First Half
news.summary: Baltimore opened the Jesse Minter era with a 41-23 rout of Indianapolis, fueled by 506 total yards, an explosive first-half offense, and a pass rush that pressured Daniel Jones on 52.9% of dropbacks. Trey Hendrickson shone in his Ravens debut with eight or nine pressures, while Flowers exited day-to-day after his career-best half—Coach Minter expressed optimism ahead of an MRI. Colts added Sauce Gardner, who locked down receivers in heavy man coverage, but fell short amid tackling woes and explosive plays allowed. Despite injuries to Flowers and Ja’Kobi Lane, Baltimore heads to face the Saints feeling strong on defense.

news.hook: Late in a tight game against the Bills, Henry To’oTo’o tackled tight end Dawson Knox and went down hard, needing help off the field with his shoulder.
news.name: Texans LB Henry To’oTo’o Out with Shoulder Injury After Bills Loss
news.summary: Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans announced Monday that linebacker Henry To’oTo’o suffered a shoulder injury in the 36-31 season-opening loss to Buffalo and will miss some time. The 25-year-old starter, who had two tackles before exiting, was seen in a sling postgame; the team hasn't decided on injured reserve yet. This adds to Houston's injury woes with absences like Tank Dell and Braden Smith, as backup Jake Hansen stepped in during the game. The Texans face the Bengals at home in Week 2, testing their linebacker depth.
